metadata.title: Supabase Apple Login on Android
metadata.description: Learn how to set up Apple Sign-In with Supabase Authentication on Android using the Capacitor Social Login plugin.

blocks.text: This guide will help you integrate Apple Sign-In with Supabase Authentication on Android. It is assumed that you have already completed:

:::note[Important]
Apple Sign-In on Android requires a backend server because Apple doesn't provide native Android support. We'll use a Supabase Edge Function as the backend.
:::
Step 1: Deploy the Backend Edge Function
First, we need to deploy the Supabase Edge Function that will handle the Apple OAuth callback.

The Apple OAuth callback endpoint must be public (no authentication required) because Apple will redirect to it. Update your

[functions.apple-signin-callback]
enabled = true
verify_jwt = false  # Important: Set to false for public OAuth callback
import_map = "./functions/apple-signin-callback/deno.json"
entrypoint = "./functions/apple-signin-callback/index.ts"

On Android, Apple Sign-In uses an OAuth redirect flow:
: The plugin is initialized with your Service ID and backend redirect URL
: Opens a browser/Chrome Custom Tab with Apple's OAuth page
: Apple redirects to your Supabase Edge Function with an authorization code
: The edge function exchanges the code for tokens using Apple's token endpoint
: The edge function redirects back to your app with the identity token
: The app receives the token and signs in to Supabase
This flow is necessary because Apple doesn't provide native Android support for Sign in with Apple.
